result:
Final answer is in `final.py`: a LIRS cache (low inter-reference recency set) whose LIR/HIR split is steered by a shadow LRU.

**Search score: 0.578 (baseline LRU 0.365). Scorer calls used: 11 of 24.**

How it works:
- **LIRS core.** Keys with short reuse distance live in the LIR set; everything else passes through a small HIR queue, so one-off scans and loops larger than the cache never displace the working set. This alone scored 0.567 and took the shifting-loops trace from 0.16 to 0.83.
- **Shadow LRU adaptation.** A plain LRU of the same capacity runs alongside. When LRU would have hit and we missed, the HIR queue grows; when we hit and LRU would not have, it shrinks. This recovered the recency trace to LRU's level (0.77 to 0.846) without touching the loop traces. The DLIRS-style ghost-hit rule I tried first misfired on loops (shifting_loops fell to 0.475), which is why the shadow signal replaced it.
- **Ghost list is 2x capacity.** Local sweeps favored larger lists, but the real split disagreed (mixed dropped from 0.265 to 0.246 at 8x), so 2x stays.

Per-trace hit rates for final.py, with the LRU baseline:

| trace | final | LRU |
|---|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.241 | 0.175 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.642 | 0.227 |
| phases | 0.648 | 0.619 |
| mixed | 0.265 | 0.158 |
| recency | 0.846 | 0.848 |
| shifting_loops | 0.828 | 0.164 |

Other candidates I scored and rejected: ARC 0.407, W-TinyLFU 0.503, hill-climbing W-TinyLFU 0.528, DLIRS 0.518. TinyLFU still edges final.py by about 0.01 on loop_and_hot and 0.005 on the two hot traces, so a frequency-aware hybrid is the remaining lead if more work is wanted.

The file passes a 300-seed invariant fuzz (store never exceeds capacity, only the requested key is added, hits match contents) and runs well under the time limit. Working files (candidates, `localtest.py`, `fuzz.py`, `sweep.py`) are left in the directory alongside `final.py`.
